findings.claim: enableSqlExpressions reads FlagSqlExpressions and then returns false on both branches, so the sqlExpressions toggle does nothing. The local variable `enabled` holds the inverse of the flag. The toggle is still registered and documented as enabling SQL expressions, and the frontend still shows the SQL expression type when it is on, so an admin who enables it gets a UI option the backend always rejects.
findings.evidence: The patch body is `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions); if enabled { return false }; return false`. The toggle is registered at pkg/services/featuremgmt/registry.go:1083 and the frontend gate is at public/app/features/expressions/types.ts:73. contribute/feature-toggles.md says to gate on IsEnabled. Proposed red test: NewExpressionQueryReader(featuremgmt.WithFeatures(FlagSqlExpressions)).ReadQuery with type sql returns 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'. Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Raised by all four seats; the code is unambiguous. The commit intent ('disable sql expressions') makes it misleading rather than a functional bug: replace the fake flag check with an explicit unconditional disable, or decide on and deprecate the toggle. Severity is Important, as three seats rated it, because of the user-facing UI/backend mismatch.

findings.claim: The new gate covers only the ReadQuery path, which runs when the expressionParser flag is on. The default legacy path (nodes.go:159 → UnmarshalSQLCommand → NewSQLCommand → sql.TablesList) is disabled only because the stub fails. Users on that path get BadRequest 'error reading SQL command' (sql-invalid-sql) rather than a disabled/not-implemented error, and parser.go logs the raw user SQL at Error level.
findings.evidence: nodes.go:123-161 sends parsing to ReadQuery only behind FlagExpressionParser. parser.go:23-29 calls the stub RunCommands, which returns errors.New("not implemented"), and logs logger.Error("error serializing sql"). sql_command.go:30-35 wraps the failure as errutil.BadRequest("sql-invalid-sql"). Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Both correctness seats rated it Minor and mattpocock rated it Important. Minor wins: nothing crashes and SQL stays blocked. The fix is cheap and folds into finding 1: put the disable check once in shared code (top of NewSQLCommand) so both paths return the same explicit error.

findings.claim: The rejection is a plain fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") rather than an errutil error with a messageID. The status code and public message are lost, and the text says 'not implemented' when the feature is actually disabled.
findings.evidence: contribute/backend/errors.md requires errutil errors with a <service>.<id> messageID and lists errutil.NotImplemented. The neighbouring code already follows the pattern: sql_command.go:27 uses errutil.BadRequest("sql-missing-query"). How the HTTP layer maps a plain error to a status code was not verified.
findings.reason: Documented standard breach from an advisory seat. Lowered from Important to Minor because the status-code impact is unverified. It is a one-line change that comes with the finding 1/2 fix.

findings.claim: No test covers the new rejection of SQL expressions, on either the ReadQuery path or the legacy path. All existing SQL tests were already t.Skip()'d, so CI exercises none of the changed behaviour.
findings.evidence: pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go has 16 tests, all t.Skip(). sql_command_test.go:9 is t.Skip(). The SQL entry in query_test.go checks the schema only.
findings.reason: A contract test that asserts SQL expressions are rejected on both parse paths would guard the fix for findings 1 and 2.

findings.claim: Dead code. DB.TablesList has no callers because parser.go uses the package-level TablesList. SQLCommand.Execute's db.QueryFramesInto (sql_command.go:96-104) is unreachable because NewSQLCommand always fails first. The stub API looks like a working DB backend.
findings.evidence: grep finds no caller of db.TablesList. parser.go:22 calls sql.TablesList. NewSQLCommand fails inside TablesList → RunCommands, so Execute is never reached.
findings.reason: ponytail: the stub mirrors the go-duck API on purpose so the engine can be restored with a small diff. Delete it if the disable becomes permanent.

findings.claim: The variable is still named duckDB but now holds the stub DB. sql_command.go:96 renamed the same variable to db, so the naming is inconsistent and implies DuckDB is still in use.
findings.evidence: parser.go:23 `duckDB := sql.DB{}` vs sql_command.go:96 `db := sql.DB{}` in the patch.
findings.reason: A one-token rename that removes a misleading reference to DuckDB.

findings.claim: The schema and docs still advertise the SQL expression: 'SQL query via DuckDB' (query.go:30), 'requires the sqlExpression feature flag' (query.go:77), the sql type in pkg/expr/query.types.json, and the toggle description in registry.go:1083 and the feature-toggles docs. The generated API schema therefore lists a query type that always fails.
findings.evidence: The patch leaves these files unchanged. superpowers cited the query.go lines; mattpocock cited docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/feature-toggles/index.md:187.
findings.reason: Outside the patch, and it depends on a product decision (permanent removal or temporary disable) that no spec settles. Track it with the toggle decision in finding 1.

findings.claim: The exported stub type DB and its methods have no doc comments, which breaks the Go Code Review Comments rule that the backend style guide adopts.
findings.evidence: db.go:9-26 in the patch declares an exported type and methods without comments.
findings.reason: ponytail: temporary stub that is likely to be deleted or replaced. Adding docs only makes sense if the stub stays.

findings.claim: enableSqlExpressions is a free function that only reads h.features. Elsewhere the file checks flags inline with h.features.IsEnabledGlobally (reader.go:160).
findings.evidence: Patch adds `func enableSqlExpressions(h *ExpressionQueryReader) bool`. reader.go:160 checks the flag inline.
findings.reason: Subsumed by finding 1: its fix deletes this function, so the style concern goes away. Advisory seat, Minor.

findings.claim: The commit subjects 'disable sql expressions' and 'Run `make update-workspace`' have no <Area>: prefix.
findings.reason: The same guide says the PR title becomes the squashed commit message, so individual branch commit subjects are not what lands. This is not a code finding.

coverage: Gate not run (benchmark mode): no build, go vet, tests, go mod tidy/verify, or lint, so every finding is reasoned and none is backed by a failing check. go.sum and go.work.sum: all seats checked them only for consistency with the go.mod removals; no hashes were verified, and OCR skipped them along with go.mod as unsupported extensions. Each seat reviewed all four Go files (reader.go, sql/db.go, sql/parser.go, sql_command.go) and read go.mod. Spec axis did not run: no spec. Standards axis ran against the contribute/ docs and .golangci.toml; the repo has no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. Untracked sandbox dotfiles in the worktree (.bashrc, .claude/, etc.) were excluded from the pinned patch because they are not part of the PR. Not checked by any seat: whether the change compiles, and the HTTP status that the ReadQuery error maps to. All seats are the same model family; no other-family reviewer was available. No Critical or Important finding from a correctness seat was rejected, so no verifier was dispatched.
